description: Exquisite handwoven silk textiles adorned with pure gold and silver Zari floral jaal, meenakari buttis, and intricate borders.
Traditional sand casting and hand-engraved brass decoratives, urns, lamps, and ritual vessels earning Moradabad the title of Pital Nagri.
Asia's largest carpet manufacturing hub specializing in hand-knotted wool and silk carpets with Persian and Indo-Tibetan motifs.
Hand-carved solid Sheesham and Acacia timber decoratives, jharokhas, and bone/brass inlay accent pieces.
Centuries-old tribal block printing using carved teak wood blocks and natural red and black vegetable dyes washed in the Baghini river.
Famous long-necked Bankura terracotta horses and indigenous non-ferrous lost-wax tribal casting by the Karmakar artisans.
Famous Baandha tie-dye handloom sarees featuring traditional Shankha, Chakra, and floral motifs woven by the Bhulia Meher community.
Rare boiled castor oil and pigment styling drawn on cloth with brass styluses alongside resist-dyed indigo-crimson geometric Ajrakh prints.
Vegetable-tanned buffalo and goat leather footwear dyed with natural babul bark and stitched with leather cord without nails.
Traditional hand-hammered bell metal Kahar dining ware, Xorai ritual trays, and brass bowls produced by local artisans in Sarthebari.
